title: Probe-Based Hallucination Monitor x Distribution Shift: When the Two Compound at Deployment

original_idea.body: Test whether a hallucination probe degrades faster than an LLM-judge under domain shift, stress-testing the probe-beats-judge claim.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: determines whether a recommended monitor is deployable under shift; clear monitoring relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probe extraction + AUROC across QA domains is guided, standard tooling; novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single focused experiment: compare probe vs judge AUROC degradation slope across OOD domains.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Third-party robustness stress-test of a published monitor; public datasets, no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap probe training on one model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Probe-under-shift is partly studied but the head-to-head probe-vs-judge degradation angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Hallucination detection under shift exists; directly stress-testing the probe-beats-judge robustness slope may be open.
